overlay-pdf.name: PDF Overlay Tool
overlay-pdf.tagline: Stamp one PDF over another — letterheads, backgrounds, and approval seals.
overlay-pdf.metaTitle: PDF Overlay Tool — Stamp One PDF Over Another Free | JaurTools
overlay-pdf.metaDescription: Overlay two PDFs online for free: stamp a letterhead, background or seal onto every page of your document. Adjust opacity, size and position. Private — runs in your browser.
overlay-pdf.keywords: pdf overlay, overlay pdf online, stamp pdf, pdf letterhead overlay, combine pdf layers
overlay-pdf.quickAnswer: Upload your main document and the PDF you want stamped over it (a letterhead, a background, a seal), choose whether it fills the page or keeps its size, set the opacity, and every page of the overlay is drawn on top of the matching page of your document.
keyFacts: The overlay PDF is drawn on top of the base PDF — like placing tracing paper over a page.
A single-page overlay is repeated on every page of the base document.
With multiple overlay pages, base page 1 gets overlay page 1, page 2 gets page 2, cycling as needed.
Opacity from 5% to 100% controls how strongly the overlay shows.
Works best with text-based PDFs; scanned-image overlays flatten into the page.
howTo: Upload the overlay PDF (letterhead, background, or stamp).
Choose "Fit to page" to stretch the overlay across the sheet, or "Actual size" to keep its dimensions and pick a position.
Build and download the combined PDF.
overlay-pdf.formula:
drawn_w = overlay_w × min(page_w / overlay_w, page_h / overlay_h)   (fit mode)
x = (page_w − drawn_w) / 2,  y = (page_h − drawn_h) / 2   (centered)

In "actual size" mode the overlay keeps its own dimensions and is placed at your chosen anchor with a 24 pt margin. Opacity blends the two layers: result = overlay × opacity + page × (1 − opacity).
overlay-pdf.workedExample: A company letterhead saved as a 1-page A4 PDF, overlaid in "Fit to page" mode at 100% opacity onto a 12-page contract: every contract page comes out on the letterhead, correctly positioned, in a single 12-page PDF — no manual copy-pasting in a desktop editor.
benefits: Apply letterheads, footers, and seals to whole documents in seconds.
Opacity control doubles as a watermark-strength dial.
Both PDFs stay vector — text remains sharp and selectable.
Position presets for actual-size stamps: corners and center.
No uploads; sensitive contracts never leave your machine.
limitations: Text-based PDFs only — complex transparency in the overlay may render differently than in a desktop viewer.
Annotations and form fields in the overlay are flattened into the page.
Both PDFs must open without a password.
Overlay pages cycle if counts differ, which may surprise mixed-length documents.
overlay-pdf.privacyNote: Both PDFs are composited locally with pdf-lib. Nothing is uploaded or stored anywhere.

faqs.q: What is the difference between overlay and watermark?
faqs.a: A watermark is usually light text or an image you add; an overlay stamps an entire PDF page — full letterheads, designed backgrounds, multi-element seals — over your document with precise positioning.
The overlay PDF is always drawn on top of the base PDF. Put your document as the base and the letterhead, background, or stamp as the overlay.

faqs.q: My overlay has 1 page but my document has 20?
faqs.a: That is the most common case: the single overlay page is repeated on all 20 pages automatically.

faqs.q: Can I make the overlay semi-transparent?
faqs.a: Yes — the opacity slider (5–100%) blends the overlay with the page beneath, from a faint background tint to fully opaque.
Base-document text stays selectable in most cases. Overlay content is flattened into each page, so treat the overlay as a picture after merging.

faqs.q: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faqs.a: Yes for the base document. But a scanned overlay is just an image — it will cover the page beneath wherever it is not transparent, so keep its opacity and size in mind.
